utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are present. Absent amongst the Defence teams, I notice Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Lazarevic, Mr. Krgovic, Mr. Haynes. Prosecution today, Prosecution team is composed of Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. Yes. The break will be at 10 minutes past 11, and then we'll have another break at 12.30. First break will be of 20 minutes; second break will be a full break of 30 minutes. We are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis, Judge Kwon being absent on official work. Are we in contact with Belgrade? We are. Good morning to you. I would like to have first confirmation from you that you can see us and that you are hearing my voice or the interpretation of what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Good morning, Your Honours. We can see and hear you, and so can the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you repeat please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Good morning, Your Honours. We can see you and hear you both in English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that confirmation. We are going to proceed with the testimony of this witness. Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You've been summoned as a Defence witness by the accused Nikolic; and before we go ahead, we need to get a confirmation from you, an undertaking, in the form of a solemn declaration that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth. The lady who is sitting next to you is going to give you, in your own language, the text of the solemn declaration. Please read it out aloud and that will be your undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Ms. Nikolic, who is the lead counsel for accused Nikolic, will be putting some questions to you; then she will be followed by others on cross-examination. Go ahead, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I will introduce myself for the record. Although we have met before, my name is Jelena Nikolic, attorney at law. I would kindly ask you to tell us what your first and last name is?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Milan Radic, son of Pavle.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When and where were you born, and how old are you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 13th of April, 1943. I'm 65 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In 1995, you were 52?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: In Malesic, the village of Malesic, near Kozluk; military post 75413.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where do you reside now?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: In Malesic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I am retired.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You were mobilised during the war in Bosnia in 1992 through to 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: To what unit and what was your position?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I was mobilised into the Zvornik Brigade in Malesic. There was a battalion there, as well as my company. We were tasked with defending the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you command a company in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you recall having given a statement to Drago Nikolic's Defence team on the 6th of April 2008?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the course of your preparation for the testimony, in the presence of our investigator, Mr. Keselj, did you have occasion to reread your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I did. I'm familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Even though there are so many hundreds of miles apart, he is answering your questions too quickly. So that creates difficulties for our interpreters. Mr. Radic, if you could possibly wait a little bit before you answer Ms. Nikolic's questions, so that you give the interpreters a chance to translate to us in English and French. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pursuant to Rule 92 ter, I will read out the entire statement of this witness since it is brief. During the war, and in July 1995, I was commander of the 3rd Company, 2nd Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade. My deputy was Petko Tomic from Malesic. The battalion command was in Malesic. The battalion commander was Sreco Acimovic from Rocevic. The battalion had a total of three companies. The companies were almost constantly at their positions. In the period after the fall of Srebrenica, due to my departure in the field, I was replaced by my deputy, Petko Tomic. In July 1995, after the fall of Srebrenica, I cannot remember the exact date, the battalion commander ordered me to prepare 12 soldiers from my company to go in the field on the frontline. That same procedure took place in the other two companies, forming a single platoon of about 36 soldiers. As I only managed to provide 11 soldiers, the battalion commander ordered me to go with them as the twelfth soldier. As far as I remember, that platoon headed towards Snagovo on the 13th of July 1995 in the afternoon. In the evening, we arrived at the Maricici position where we spent the night of the 13th to the 14th of July 1995. We remained there the following day and one more night. On the 15th of July 1995, around 11.00 a.m., we left that position in Maricici. There were no combat activities with the BH Army in at that region. They broke through our lines and left towards Baljkovica. On the 15th of July 1995, when we left the position in Maricici, I thought that we were going back to the battalion; however, the order was to continue towards Baljkovica where we arrived in the afternoon. We were immediately deployed along the frontline. Those two days were very hard. There was heavy combat until the 16th of July 1995 when the corridor was opened, and the Muslim forces crossed the defence lines. After the corridor had been opened, we went through the woods towards Caparde, and we stayed there for three more days since we could not go back towards Zvornik. Crni Vrh had been sealed off or closed. Three days later, we returned to the battalion. All that time while I was at the frontlines, I had no communication with the 2nd Battalion and the commander, Acimovic. After the 16th of July 1995, I returned to the battalion, and my deputy, Petko Tomic, reported what had happened in my absence. On that occasion, he did not report anything special, and I here by declare with full responsibility that my deputy never informed me or mentioned to me the existence of a telegram from the Zvornik Brigade command requesting men to carry out executions. I have no knowledge about that from anyone else. I'm also sure that if something like that had happened, my deputy, Petko Tomic, would have informed me. This concludes my reading of the statement pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, do you recognise your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The facts stated therein, are they true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do they truly reflect what you would testify before this Tribunal if asked about the events described in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point, Your Honour, I seek to tender the statement of witness Milan Radic, number 3D477.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection from Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. From the other Defence teams? All right. The document is being admitted. Yes. Do you have any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I have a few additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, how many soldiers were there in your company and where was it exactly in mid-July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: My company was about 140 strong. It was in Malesic at the defence lines in the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How many trenches were there for your company?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, around 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: While you were at the positions, what was your regular communication of your company with the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: We had wire connection. There was the company command, and we had land lines that we could use to communicate with the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Are these induction telephone?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's what they are called.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you ever communicate with the battalion command using Motorolas or radio devices?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you have a Motorola?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So you were not using it, if I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: We were not using it because the land line was more secure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: While your company was at the positions in Maricici in mid-July in 1995, did you communicate with the battalion command in Malesic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I had no communication with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that the battalion commander ordered that 12 soldiers from your company be sent to some frontlines. Do you remember how that particular order was conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I was told that by my signalsman. It was sent from the battalion communications department down to the company, and my signalsman at the company conveyed that to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: At the time, what was the situation like at the frontlines that were held by the part of your company that left towards Malesic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Do you mean Malesic or Maricici?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Maricici?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Maricici. Well, when we left from Maricici, we arrived there in the course of the night. We were then deployed along the frontline. We spent the night there. Perhaps we arrived there around midnight. When the day broke, we stayed another 12 hours; then Mr. Obrenovic came from the Zvornik Brigade command and ordered us to move forward. My soldiers went towards the left. On the right-hand side, there were quite many of our soldiers. We set out, and after some 500 metres, the Muslims opened fire upon us. They were relatively close in the forest, and they clashed with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Radic. This was already described in your statement. I apologise for interrupting you, but I want to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How did you learn of Srebrenica's fall?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: While I was in Malesic with the company, people were talking about it and you could hear it from the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In mid-July, when you were at the frontline, did you have any information about the situation in other battalions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: During that period, while you were away from your company, do you know whether there was any fighting at the frontlines where the rest of your company had been left?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: There was none.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: When I returned to the company.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did your deputy report it to you upon your return, Mr. Tomic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say: "After the corridor was opened, we went through the woods towards Caparde, and we spent three more days there." Do you remember when you precisely returned to your company?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you what the exact date was. It was a long time ago. I can't tell you exactly. We stayed three days in Caparde. We couldn't go through because the forests around us were full of Muslims. There was a danger of being attacked.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: While you were away, who commanded the 3rd Company in the period while you were at the frontlines?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: In my company?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Petko Tomic, my deputy.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, when you returned to your company, what did Petko Tomic report to you, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I remember that when I returned he told me that things were fine, that there were no attacks, that the trenches are fully manned. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was your relationship with Petko Tomic, the deputy company commander, in the course of July 1995 and afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: We were on good terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your statement you say that, upon your return to the battalion, and I quote: "On that occasion, he didn't report to me anything in particular. I state with full responsibility that my deputy never of informed me of any telegram for the Zvornik Brigade requesting men to carry out executions." Did you learn anything about the existence of such a telegram from any other battalion member, including the battalion commander, Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I state with full responsibility that during the time I was at the company, no telegrams of that nature arrived. Had it arrived, I would have been informed by someone. I have never heard of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This was already in the statement, Ms. Nikolic. If you look at paragraph 4 or part 4, the line before the last: "I have no knowledge about that from anyone else."

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, do you know, by chance, whether the other companies of your battalion received such a request?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you attend a meeting with other company commanders at the battalion command after your return in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you remember approximately when was the first time that you met with the investigators of Drago Nikolic's team?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I think about a year and a half ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did they introduce themselves to you on that occasion, and how did they do that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, they told me that they were Defence lawyers of Drago Nikolic. There was Radovan Keselj and a woman called Nevenko, I don't know her last name. They were the two who -- who contacted me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you mean investigators or Defence lawyers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I don't remember how they introduced themselves. I think they said "investigators."

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what they asked you when you first met them, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, they asked me to state my name and to say that I was commander in Malesic. And after that, we discussed this issue of telegram, whether I had received before I went into the field, whether my deputy had received it to send people. But I said what I said in my statement, that I had been on the frontline, and that after I had returned, my deputy told me that nothing of the sort happened and nobody informed me of anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: During July 1995, did you know anything at all about any prisoners housed in the school in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Rocevic is 20 kilometres from Malesic, and I didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Also, in July 1995, did you know anything about the fact that these prisoners were later on executed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information today about that?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] ... we have a problem with the ... correct this problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a problem? I am not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes. We don't receive the image anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the background, still I'm hearing voices. I see from the registrar a note that we have -- we don't even have the image anymore. I can see the image on your monitor, and I have the image myself. Can I ask the witness to repeat what he may have answered to the question put to him by Ms. Nikolic. The question was the following: "Also, in July 1995, did you know anything about the fact that these prisoners were later on executed. And you said: "No, I didn't." Then she asked you: "Do you have any information today about those events?" And what was your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't give any answer due to the interruptions. Nowadays, by following the Seselj trials and the witnesses who testified that is the way through which I heard and learned about executions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, in the event that there was a request to have members of the 2nd Battalion to take part in these executions, would that be something that would -- that you would remember even to this date?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Of course, I would, but I wouldn't allow any member of my company to go out there and do such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Had such a request existed, would your deputy, Petko Tomic, conveyed it to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I said, if it had existed, he would have certainly conveyed it to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no questions for this witness in the examination-in-chief. Thank you, Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nikolic. Any of the other Defence teams wish to cross-examine this witness? I see no reaction. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you, good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And good morning to you, Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My name is Kweku Vanderpuye; and on behalf of the Prosecution, I'm going to put some questions to you in relation to your testimony and the statement dated 6 April 2008. If there's anything that I ask you that is unclear, please let me know so that I can try to rephrase it in a way that we can better understand one another?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I suppose, right off the bat, I want to ask you: You indicated that you that Major Obrenovic came at some point while you were in Maricici and ordered you to move on, and I just want to get from you at approximately what time it was that that occurred?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Around 1.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you personally see Major Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, Petko Tomic was your deputy company commander in July 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I think you indicated on direct examination that you have since remained on good terms?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And have you spoken to Petko Tomic about the events of July 1995, and specifically about the telegram, the prisoners, the school, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, we didn't because we had no knowledge of the existence of any telegram, so there was nothing to discuss. We never received any telegram, and we also didn't hear anything about the school in Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with what Petko Tomic has said about the telegram, about the prisoners, and the school, and Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, he probably said that he also did not receive any telegram. I suppose this is what he stated. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you speak to Petko Tomic at all regarding these matters prior to your discussion -- or rather, prior to your statement of 6 April?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And when was the last time you spoke to Petko Tomic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Petko Tomic is even today here with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Did you speak to him this morning?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is it your testimony, then, that you've never spoken to Petko Tomic about your contacts with the Defence or his contacts with the Defence; that is, the Nikolic Defence in this case?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No. We are just good friends. We spend time together. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When was the first time you became acquainted with the idea that a telegram was sent to the 2nd Battalion in July 1995, calling for the formation of an execution squad?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I heard that from the investigators who came to see me and to ask for my statement. They asked me about this telegram, and that was 18 months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when you met with them the first time, you told them that you had no information about a telegram or prisoners at the school or the fact that they had been executed; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I didn't tell them anything because I didn't know anything either about the telegram or about the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that was 24th March 2007?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, more or less. I do not recall the exact date, but that was a year and a half ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You then met with them again on 23rd June 2007; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall any dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You remember that you met with them on three occasions, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, what I'm referring to is the second of those three occasions. The date that we have and been provided with is 23rd June 2007. Now, in relation to the second time that you met with the Defence, did you provide them with any information different than you provided them with the first time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, it was all the same. Whatever is written in my statement, that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to the second time you were interviewed, were you asked any questions different from the questions you were asked on the first occasion, with respect to your knowledge of the events in Rocevic in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did they provide you with any information at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Did you say, "Yes, they did"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. On the first occasion that you met with the Defence, what did the investigators tell you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse, with our permission, your client has left the courtroom for a short while. I take it we can proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We can, Your Honour. Thank you very much for alerting me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this question was already put to the witness in direct examination, and he gave an answer to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think I'm entitled to ask the question because it's cross-examination, even if it was asked on direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I take it if it's leading you to another question, then, yes; but, otherwise, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What information -- what did the investigators tell you concerning these events on the first occasion that you met with them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I told them that I was the company commander. They asked me if I had received any telegram. I had already told them that I never received it in terms of sending men to execute the Bosniaks. That was while I was on the line. And when I went into the field, my deputy, Petko Tomic, replaced me, and he repeated that he didn't receive any telegram either.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, did they tell you what form the telegram came in?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, it never arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I want to focus you on, if I may, is what information was provided to you by the investigators that came to see you on the first occasion you met with them. So what I would like to know is what did they tell you in particular about this telegram, such as, what form it was in. Did they tell you that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This witness has been asked two or three times in the same manner and about the same issue, and he gave the answer that he is capable of giving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is different. This is a different kind of question. It specifically refers to whether it was put to the witness the form of this telegram and other details. So please, if you could answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They persistently asked me whether I had received the telegram while I was in the company, and my answer was always no, in any form or shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Did they tell you when it was this telegram was supposedly -- supposed to have arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did they tell you whether or not the telegram was transmitted by radio or by telephone; that is, hard wire?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you that they only asked me if I had received this telegram. I said I didn't, and they didn't ask me anything else about it. I cannot be asked questions about something that I never received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. How long did you meet with the investigators on the first occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, between half an hour and an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you met with them after that on two other occasions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in relation to the second occasion, you said that the content essentially of the interview was the same; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: The same, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Same questions, same answers, same information; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that is when I gave my statement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please turn off his microphone when he is not speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I will. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The information that we have is that you met with the Defence on three separate occasions, and on the third occasion is the date of your statement which was April 6th. Do you have that recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I remember these two or three occasions, but I cannot tell you exactly how many times. Approximately three times, I'm not sure, but that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you would agree that, as a company commander, it's important to know about the disposition of your troops in any given time; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You had 140 troops and they were in roughly 14 trenches, I think you said?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it's important as a commander, isn't it, to know how many you have, how many troops you have, where they are, what they are doing, and especially when they are placed in a condition of heightened readiness; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you need to know this as a commander because that information is essential to your ability to command those troops?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's vital to their being able to carry out tasks that they are assigned; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's also important to the broader interests of the brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it's equally important to the deputy commander of a company; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, as a commander, it's important that you know about anything that could threaten the positions that are manned by your company; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had our area of responsibility, there were 14 trenches, and the crucial thing for me was to guard this line within my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of securing that area of responsibility, it's important, of course, that you know what the movements of the enemy are, their number, their location and so on; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, we are far away from one another so we couldn't know their movements and their numbers because the line that separated us was -- made the distance between us about two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, your company was made up of soldiers that were from villages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one intervention regarding the transcript. On page 21, line 3, the witness said that they were separated in trenches, and this was not recorded in the transcript, more than two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nikolic. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your company was made up of soldiers that were primarily from villages in and around Rocevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No. My company was made up of the residents of Malesic. There was no person from Rocevic in my company. They had their own company.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. I think you indicated that Malesic was about 20 kilometres or so from Rocevic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you returned to the brigade or -- I'm sorry, you returned to the battalion after the 16th -- first of all, do you recall about what date -- how many days after the 16th that you returned?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I said that I left approximately on the 13th and that I came back on the 16th or the 17th, which means that I spent five days in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you came back, you spoke to Petko Tomic, your deputy; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you were informed at that time that there had been no fighting while you were away; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Not in our area of responsibility because our company was deployed to guard the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He told you that things were fine; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He told you that the trenches were manned; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Some men were in the trenches and those who were not on duty were allowed to go home on leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did he tell you that the battalion had been placed on a heightened state of readiness while you were away?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you ever learn that the battalion had been placed on a heightened state of readiness at any time, while at any time following the fall of Srebrenica up until your return on the 16th or 17th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you said that he didn't tell you that prisoners had been brought to the school in Rocevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: He didn't tell me anything, and I have no idea about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know somebody by the name of Milan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with who the president of the local commune in Rocevic was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you then or have you heard since -- well, let me ask you a different way. Did you then or have you heard since about a woman that was injured, I believe shot, in and around the time that you were away from your battalion in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to state the ethnicity of this woman? I think it would help the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe she was a Serb woman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I believe so, too, but I don't know whether the witness was expecting this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you hear about a Serb woman that was shot and injured in and around Rocevic during the time that you were away from your battalion in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know somebody by the name of Petko Tanaskovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that name, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you then or do you now have information that prisoners were, in fact, brought to the school in Rocevic and that, in fact, some of them were killed there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: As I said, I only heard about it when the Vojislav Seselj trial was taking place. Some witnesses mentioned that, but, otherwise, I have no other information about the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you were never told by your deputy, Petko Tomic, that there were prisoners taken from the school and executed in Kozluk; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You said before that you would never have allowed anybody in your company to participate in an execution. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I can state that, with full responsibility, I would never have allowed anyone from my company to go and execute any prisoners. I claim that such a thing did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you ever made aware that 2nd Battalion soldiers actually participated in the detention and execution of these prisoners in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I was not. I didn't learn anything about Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know somebody by the name of Milorad Ristanovic? He is a soldier in the 3rd Company of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Milorad Ristanovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does he go by the name of also "Beco"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, that's not the one. That's not the one. I know Milorad Ristanovic. He went to America, he lives there now, but he is not the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that he was at Kozluk and participated in the execution there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, anyway, what was your objection? Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know somebody by the name of Ljubo Ristanovic? He is also a soldier in the 3rd company, 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, no. I don't know a Ljubo Ristvanovic. I know Stanko Ristanovic, but not a Ljubo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, Ljubo Ristanovic is a member of the 3rd company of the 2nd battalion. His father's name is Pero. Did you ever hear that he was -- that he was at the execution site in Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I never heard of such a thing. I can guarantee you he would never do such a thing. I know him as a quiet man. I know that because I can guarantee for those who were at the frontlines. I don't know what the people were doing while on leave. However, for this person, I guarantee he would not do such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you do know who I'm talking about then; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: We call him Stanko Ristanovic. I don't know whether his name is Ljubo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Do you know someone by the name of Dragan Jovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know that Dragan Jovic was a member of the 2nd battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: But not in my company.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Not in your company, that's right. You know who I'm talking about then?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know that a person with such a first and last name was not in my company, as far as I can remember. As to whether he was in the battalion with the 1st or 2nd Company, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You never heard that Dragan Jovic, member of the 2nd Battalion, was at the school and at the execution site; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I did not hear of such a thing, I swear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know somebody called Zoran Simanic? He is a member of the 2nd Battalion, he is in the reconnaissance platoon, and he is the commander. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You never heard that he was at the execution site either, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know somebody by the name of Radivoje Jekic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you have no information that he was involved in these events at all; right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear of or I was never informed of any of the people that I know taking part in the executions. This was far from the place where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have just a few questions in the area of the communications of the battalion, if I could -- I think you indicated the break time is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long do you expect you need more?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think maybe ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then we'll have the break now. May I ask our registrar over there how long, after this witness finishes the testimony, how much time do they require over there, technically, in particular, to get the next witness and start him off.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] The next witness is here, so we can ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] The next witness is here, so we can start immediately after we finish with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then we'll have the break now. You will continue immediately after, Mr. Vanderpuye, and we start with the next witness immediately after that. Thank you. Twenty minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to confirm, once more, that you are receiving me and that the witness is receiving interpretation in his own language?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour. We are receiving image and sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we can proceed. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will be much shorter than the ten minutes I had anticipated, I hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the Trial Chamber will be grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, you know that your commander, Sreco Acimovic, testified in this case between the 20th and the 22nd of June of this year publicly, and that Mitar Lazarevic, the general affairs clerk of the 2nd Battalion command, testified in this case on the 26th of June 2007. Are you saying, and correct me if I'm wrong, that you never heard about the fact that they testified in these proceedings about the incidents or the occurrences in Rocevic and in Kozluk with regard to these Muslim prisoners that were executed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I only recently heard that Sreco Acimovic testified in The Hague. I wasn't particularly interested though. It was recently that I learned that he was in The Hague. And as for Mitar Lazarevic, this is the first time I hear it from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, you didn't learn that Sreco Acimovic had testified through the Seselj case, so when is it that you learned that he testified in this case?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that he testified in this case. I only know that he went to testify in The Hague, but I didn't know which case it concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When did you hear that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Perhaps a month ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And from whom?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: We were sitting in a bar, and a neighbour of mine told me that he heard Sreco went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What is your neighbour's name, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: Mida, Milorad Sakotic, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What did he tell you about what Mr. Acimovic testified?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: He didn't tell me anything about that. He only said that he heard, too, that Sreco went to The Hague. We didn't discuss that any further. We didn't discuss the reason for his going there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The Prosecution has information from two witnesses independently placing Milorad Ristanovic, that is, of the 3rd Company, 2nd Battalion; and Ljubo Ristanovic, the 3rd Company, 2nd Battalion, as being involved in these events at the school or at the execution site. Is it your position that you deny any knowledge of members -- of the participation of members of either your battalion or your company in these events?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Nikolic. One moment, Mr. Radic, one moment. Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question has already been put to the witness, and he has answered it on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You wish to comment, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I do. I asked him whether or not he knew. I'm asking him now whether or not he denies that they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will allow the question being somewhat different from the previous one. Please try to stick to the question and answer the question and nothing else, Mr. Radic, please. Do you wish the question to be repeated to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could he please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to know whether or not you deny that members of your battalion and, in fact, members of your company participated in the events concerning the school and the execution of prisoners in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC
utterances.text: I state with full responsibility that I don't know of any people from my company taking part in the liquidations of those Muslims. I am only referring to the people from my company. I don't know about the rest of the battalion. I don't know of a single man from the company going to execute anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Is there re-examination, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it there are no questions from the Bench? No. Mr. Radic, we've come to the end of your testimony. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having been kind enough to travel to Belgrade or wherever the videolink testimony is taking place, I and I also wish you a safe journey back home. Our registrar will now proceed to get the next witness ready.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, do you have any documents that you wish to tender, apart from the statement which has already been admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No other documents. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You had indicated a series of documents you would have used with this witness, but you haven't used any.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you don't have any documents either. So we are finished with the testimony of Mr. Radic, and I think we can proceed with the testimony of Mr. Tomic. Let me just check that he is there. Yes, he is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Dobar dan, Gospodine Tomic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I will switch on to English, and I want to make sure you are receiving interpretation of what I am saying in your own language. Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You have been summoned to give evidence by the Defence team of Mr. Nikolic. And according to our Rules, before you start your testimony, you are required to make a solemn declaration in the sense that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth. The gentle lady sitting next to you will give you the text of the solemn declaration in your own language. Please read it out aloud so that we can hear you, and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Tomic. Ms. Nikolic will introduce herself, will put some questions to you, and after that, we'll proceed with cross-examination, if any. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tomic.

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My name is Jelena Nikolic, attorney at lawyer, appearing on behalf of Drago Nikolic. We both speak the same language; therefore, I would kindly ask you to wait before answering so that the interpreters would have sufficient time to interpret everything we said and to have a correct transcript. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Please statement your first and last name for the record?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Petko Tomic. I was born on the 7th of October, 1955, in Malesic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you reside in Malesic?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How long have you lived in Malesic?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Fifty-three years, since the day I was born.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your occupation is?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I am a construction machinery operator.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where are you employed? What is the name of the company?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: In Novi Sad --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the name of the company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you repeat the name of the company, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Backa Put in Novi Sad. Vojvodina Put is a bigger company that owns Backa Put.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: For how long have you been working for Backa Put in Novi Sad?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Since March 1977.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How far is Novi Sad from Malesic, the place where you live?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Around 170 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were you mobilised during the war?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In what unit?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: The Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were you in any particular battalion or company?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I was in the 3rd Company in Malesic that belonged to a battalion. I did not change my location during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You are referring to the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: There were eight battalions there. I forgot where I was and who commanded what at what time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember giving a statement to Drago Nikolic's Defence team in April 2008?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I do. I remember that it was more than a year ago. I don't know whether it was April, but sometime in the course of last year.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Before going to Belgrade to testify, did you have occasion to reread your statement in the presence of Mr. Radovan Keselj?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you check the date on the cover page of the statement?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I think it said the 6th of April. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to Rule 92 ter, I will read out your entire statement, Mr. Tomic, given that it is short.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My name is Petko Tomic, and I live in Malesic near Zvornik. I have been employed for almost 30 years in Novi Sad in Vojvodina Put in Serbia. During the war, I was a member of the 3rd Company, 2nd Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade. I was a deputy commander of the 3rd Company, 2nd Battalion. The commander of the 3rd Company was Milan Radic, and the commander of the 2nd Battalion was Sreco Acimovic. The battalion command was located in Malesic, and our company was away from Malesic at the positions that is the combat lines. I remember that in July 1995, after the fall of Srebrenica, a group of 12 men from our company, including Commander Radic, received an order to go to the positions in order to secure the lines that were rather long. They were sent to Maricici. When Commander Radic departed, I remained at the company as his deputy. We were placed at a high level of readiness, and we were at our usual positions. We stayed on the line day and night since the order was to defend the line due to the proximity of the enemy. During that period after the fall of Srebrenica, while I was replacing Commander Radic who was absent, at the company I was not contacted by the battalion commander, Sreco Acimovic, either by phone or personally, in order to inform me about the existence of any telegram. I have never heard about the existence of any telegram from the Zvornik Brigade command requesting men to participate in executions. I have no knowledge about that. The position where I was is far from the rear. I have no knowledge about those events, and I never heard that anyone exerted any pressure on the battalion commander, Sreco Acimovic, to select men to carry out executions. With this, I conclude the reading of the statement pursuant to 92 ter rule.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, do you recognise your statement?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, entirely.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Are the facts contained in your statement true?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do they fully reflect what you would have testified before this Tribunal had you been asked to describe the events concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The quality of the sound via videolink is very bad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know if we can do anything about that, certainly not from our side, but our registrar there perhaps can have a chat with the technicians. If I could ask the interpreters what the problem really is. Is it low volume? What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's barely audible at times, but there's a lot of background noise. I don't know where it's coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. I suppose Ms. Alvarez has heard that, if she can give us feedback whether she can improve the reception.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, I'll see if I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go on in the meantime. The witness if he could kindly speak into the microphone, and the technicians try to eliminate any background noise that there might be. You had a question, Mr. Tomic, which was a simple one. I'll read it out for you. Ms. Nikolic asked you whether the statement, the statement that was read out, fully reflects what you would have testified before this Tribunal had you been asked to describe the events concerned mentioned therein. Would you have stated the same things in other words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would say the same. What has been said, I would repeat that before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Back to you, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for your assistance. At this point, Your Honour, I would like to request the statement of this witness, 3D478, to be admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would like to defer the Prosecution's position with respect to this statement. My colleague, with respect to the last witness, essentially took the witness through the contents of the entire statement. To the extent that she does that in this case, we would be objecting to the admission of the statement as cumulative and unnecessary under the circumstances. But if it covers new matter, we will have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sure that Ms. Nikolic has got the message. We didn't stop her before. I suppose she will restrict herself to putting questions that haven't been already answered in the statement that she wishes to tender. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I'm going to ask the questions that were not asked when the witness gave his statement, and also the ones that I believe need and require additional clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, how many soldiers were there in your company and in how many trenches, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I think that there were 14 trenches and about 130 or 140 soldiers, but it varied afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, how did your company communicate with the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, we had those telephones, induction telephones.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you communicate with the battalion command perhaps via radios or Motorola or anything else?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, there were radio sets for a time, and there were Motorolas as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How often did you use radio sets or Motorolas?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. We had -- the two of us had the Motorolas, or three of us, and we always carried them with us. We also had radio sets. The communications officer used it to communicate sometimes. Sometimes we had them, sometimes we didn't during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What devices did you use more often among those that you just named?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: The induction telephones.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How did you learn about the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, when Commander Radic called me, I was off duty. He called me because he had to go to re-enforce the line, and that something had happened a couple of days later. We heard that Srebrenica had fallen, but I cannot remember now who I heard it directly from. It was in the media too.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any information directly from your battalion command in your company about the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Not on that day; however, the command heard about this later.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did they inform your company about this?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: They only told the company to reinforce the line because the enemy was close and might attack our combat line.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any information about the movement of the BH Army column retreating from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, when Radic went to the frontline, we heard that they were withdrawing from Srebrenica over there, but that was the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who told you that or how you received this information?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that most probably we, Radic and I, spoke; but I'm not sure. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information about the situation in other battalions in those days in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because children were right behind our lines and all I took care of was my company.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were you involved in any combat activities in July 1995 along the line defended by your company? I'm referring to the period when Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, there was just sporadic shooting, nothing serious.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the closest battles were?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, in that part, Maricici and this area, Baljkovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you spoke on the phone, on this induction phone, with Commander Acimovic in mid-July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: No. I never had an opportunity to talk to him directly over the phone.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when your company commander, Milan Radic, returned from the line?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: He was on the line four or five days; but at what time and when, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: While Radic was on the line in Maricici, did you have any contacts with him?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And what did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Just about the situation over there and the situation where we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And what did you tell your commander, Radic, on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: That nothing was happening, that we were on the line one hundred percent, and that we are expecting something to happen any day.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When your commander returned from Maricici, did you report to him about the events in the company?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, we just talked normally about what had been happening while he was away and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: During July 1995, what were relations between you and your commander, Milan Radic, on the 3rd Company?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the answer from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, please, Mr. Tomic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] we were always on good terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you a general question. How did you receive information from the battalion command in your company? Was it in writing or orally?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Orally, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, were you present in mid-July at any meeting with other company commanders at the battalion command headquarters where the telegram was discussed and where Mitar Lazarevic was?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I don't know where Mitar was, and I didn't attend these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And are you aware of any such meeting being held at the battalion command with other company commanders and deputy commanders?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting the investigators of Drago Nikolic's Defence team, and can you tell us approximately when that took place?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, I think about a half -- a year and a half ago for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did they introduce themselves to you?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What did they tell you who they were?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: They told me they were investigators, they told me their names, and then they asked me a couple of questions on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the questions that you were asked on this first occasion - I mean the investigators from Drago Nikolic's Defence team - and can you tell us where the meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: It took place in my house, and the first thing that they asked me was about this telegram and whether I knew of it; and they also asked me whether we had singled out men to go and carry out some executions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did they ask you about what you know about prisoners and the events in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to July 1995. I'm asking you if you knew about the prisoners held in the school in Rocevic in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I didn't know anything at all. This became known maybe a month later because this is some ten kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Also, in July 1995, did you know anything about these prisoners being executed in Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. It might have been six months later, or one year later, that I heard of it on TV and read about it in the press.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell us how far were your -- how far apart were your company and the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Approximately one kilometre or maybe one and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you hear and do you know --

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, my colleague is warning me that we might have a correction for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Excuse us, Mr. Tomic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Page 41, line 12: These prisoners were being kept at the school in Rocevic, or held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Instead of "health," it's "held." Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know Vojo Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you see Vojo Lazarevic in the course of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I can't recall, but it is quite likely that we saw each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you did, did you exchange a few words?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Vanderpuye, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness said that it was quite likely that they saw each other and there's no indication -- I think the next question is without foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You are right. You can rephrase the question: "When you met or when you saw each other, did you exchange any conversations?" So, Mr. Tomic, if you've been following, you said that you can't recall, but it is quite likely that you did see Mr. Lazarevic, Vojo Lazarevic, in the course of July 1995. When you saw him, did you speak to him or did he speak to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I see Vojo frequently. Whether I saw him in July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. We are talking about July 1995 only.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember exactly. It is very likely. Since he was at the battalion command, it is quite likely that we saw each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question is not only whether you maybe saw each other but whether you spoke to each other on that occasion when you probably saw each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About what? I don't know. We always talked as friends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let's move, Ms. Nikolic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In those friendly conversations, did you ever hear from Vojo Lazarevic that he sent a request for the 2nd Battalion that their soldiers take part in the execution of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear anything of the sort in July 1995 from Mitar Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Had such a request been made, would you have mentioned it to your company commander, Milan Radic?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. At this point, I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do any of the other Defence teams wishes to cross-examine this witness? I hear no response. Mr. Vanderpuye, Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long do you think you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would guess about a half an hour, maybe shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't think you can restrict it to 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thank you. You will be doing one of us a favour in other words, because after 12.30 we have a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I proceed, yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Tomic. My name is Kweku Vanderpuye, and on behalf of the Prosecution, I will put some questions to you in relation to your statement in your direct testimony. If there's anything that I ask you that is unclear to you, please let me know and I will try to rephrase it in a way that we can better understand one another. Okay?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: That's fine, and good afternoon to you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Sir, according to your statement, you were interviewed by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were interviewed by the Defence on three occasions: 24th March 2007, 23rd June 2007, and 6th of April 2008. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you are aware that those are the same dates that your commander, Milan Radic, was interviewed by the Defence, about these same events; right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you know that because you've spoken to Mr. Radic about his interviews with the Defence; right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: We did talk in the meantime because we are from the same village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, I'll not talking about casual conversation. I'm talking about specifically the fact that Mr. Radic was interviewed by the Defence, that you were interviewed by the Defence, and that you two spoke about those interviews?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: No. Since I work in Novi Sad, I also work on most Saturdays; therefore, I arrive late in the evening on Saturday and I depart the day after on Sunday. Therefore, I do not move about the village much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you've not spoken to Mr. Radic about the fact that you were interviewed by the Defence; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
