utterances.text: No, not then. Later, we talked in a bar. I heard from him that he was visited by the Defence, and then I told him they visited me, too. That was the extent of our conversation that we had in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you never spoke about what it was you were interviewed concerning; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, an intervention for the transcript. Page 45 line 19, the witness said they spoke in the bar, not in the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But please, next time, wait until he finishes answering the question, and then you can raise the transcript. This applies to everyone. Try to avoid interrupting the process, if it's just a transcript error, until at least the question has been put and answered. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. You probably need to repeat the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You never spoke with Mr. Radic about what it was you were interviewed concerning by the Defence; is that your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: It is, yes. We only talked about the fact that we were both visited by the investigators, and they were only asking questions about the telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you did discuss the telegram with Mr. Radic, that time you met him in the bar?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I take it that you know that he said that he wasn't aware of any such telegram; right? You knew that after you met with him and spoke with him?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We heard about the telegram from the media and the stories which were going around after the events had taken place. It was last year that we discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, I believe you said that you heard about the prisoners in the school and the events concerning those prisoners, their execution, and so on, about a month after the fact; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, I said a month or two months later or maybe a fortnight later; but, in any case, afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Maybe even up to half a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So anywhere from a fortnight after to about a half a year; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes, more or less. I can't recall everything. It's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And at the time that you learned about these events, your commander also learned about these events; right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, weren't you with your commander immediately following these events after the 16th or 17th of July 1995 on out?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And the two of you never discussed what you learned in the press following these events?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You never discussed with your commander --

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Which two?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you and your commander. You never discussed with your commander what you learned about the events that occurred in Rocevic in July 1995 when or close to when you first learned about it?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you. Since I was deputy company commander, I wasn't with the commander all the time. We just met on that he occasion, and it is my company commander that he communicated with, not myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I take it that when you found out that there had been executions in Rocevic, a fortnight or so after the events themselves, you spoke about that with your commander. Are you saying that that never occurred?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a problem or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am sorry, sir. Did you hear the question?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I did. That conversation never took place within myself and the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. So, when you found out that there had been executions anywhere from 14 to 20 kilometres from your positions manned by your men, you never brought that to the attention of the commander even though you heard about it in the press. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: No. I'm trying to say that I talked to the commander only in exceptional circumstances if my "komandir" was absent. I had no communication with the "komandant."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry. When I am talking about the "commander," I'm talking about Milan Radic, just so you know who we're talking about. I apologise if I've caused some confusion. I mean Milan Radic.

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what you mean. Then there was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you spoke to him about the events that you learned concerning what occurred in Rocevic when you learned about it; right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if I talked to him. It was almost at the end of the war, and I left for Novi Sad immediately afterwards to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sir, I'm given to understand from your testimony that you have no information or had no information at the time that there were prisoners that had been brought to the Rocevic School and that were thereafter detained, transported, and executed in Kozluk; is that the substance of your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: My testimony is that I didn't know at all that they were held at the school. I didn't know they were executed until half a year later or so. I can't remember when it was that I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you learn at any point, sir, that members of the 3rd Company of the 2nd Battalion, your unit, were involved in the detention, transportation, or execution of those prisoners? Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: That didn't take place and no one from the 3rd Company took part.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the name of Milorad Ristanovic and Ljubo Ristanovic? Do you recognise those names, sir? They are both in the 3rd Company of the 2nd Battalion, your unit.

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Those two individuals have been identified independently as having to do with the events at the school and/or the execution. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you. This Ljubo Ristanovic was in a different unit. Milorad Ristanovic, I can't tell you anything about him. I don't believe that happened that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the name Ljubo Ristanovic, son of Pero? Do you recognise that name?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you are saying that person wasn't in your unit; right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: He was, he was, but only about a year. Otherwise, I know the man. Of course, I know him from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just bear with me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] but he certainly did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I know that it's 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I can go for five more minutes, I think I could be finished. I don't want to detain anybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. It's all right. Let's go on for five more minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You think you have re-examination so far as least, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not for the time being, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sir, this Ljubo Ristanovic that you referred to, do you know how he is referred to, what his nickname is?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Stanko. We call him Stanko.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And were you aware then or have you become aware that other members of the 2nd Battalion were also involved in the events at the school and the execution, the transport, I should say, and execution of prisoners in Rocevic? The execution was in Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You testified that you did receive communications from the battalion command orally for the most part. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Via the induction telephone, orally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to the communications that you received, it's fair to say that you did occasionally receive them in written form; right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, the war lasted for three or four years, and there were eight battalions there. I don't know which battalion used what at what point in time, and if they used written orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, sir, at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it would have been fair to the witness to determine the framework, temporal framework, about the battalion communications, but the witness has already answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. No re-examination, I take it? Questions? Questions? Mr. Tomic, we have no further questions for you which means you are free to go. Thank you for having cooperated and come over to give testimony; and if you have to travel back to your home residence, have a safe journey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you and I wish all the best to you. I wish to say good-bye to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Message received. Yes. The communication videolink communication can be terminated now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, you had tendered the statement, 92 ter statement. No objection, I take it, now?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, there isn't, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So it's admitted. No further documents, I take it, either from --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We stand adjourned until tomorrow. We are going to start with the expert tomorrow, aren't we? Yes Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I know the Court is very anxious to adjourn, but could I just say the Gvero team have been working very feverishly and can say that we have no opposition to the 65 ter motion of General Miletic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much. There also being no opposition from the Prosecution, we can deal with it tomorrow. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
